<teammate-message teammate_id="Engineer" color="blue" summary="placeBlock curse investigation — found a real lead: a Fabric mod named "ledger" is loaded server-side">
Investigation done, no code touched. Found something concrete — worth reading before the rest.

(d) SERVER-SIDE CHECK, done first because it turned up gold: `datapack list` via RCON shows 6 datapacks, including **"ledger (Fabric mod)"**. Ledger is a real, known Fabric server mod (Rubydesic/Ledger, CoreProtect-equivalent for Fabric) — its whole job is logging every block change for admin rollback/inspection. Confirmed `/ledger` is a live command (RCON recognized the prefix, rejected bare `ledger`/`ledger help` as incomplete — real subcommand tree exists, needs `ledger search`/`ledger inspect`/`ledger rollback` etc.). I stopped guessing exact syntax through the RCON wrapper (kept hitting quoting issues indirectly) — you have direct console/RCON access and Ledger's own config/db, much faster for you to check than me blind-guessing subcommands. THIS is my top lead, not a coincidence I'd bet on: a mod that logs+can-rollback every block change, if its write is synchronous or contends under load, would produce EXACTLY this symptom (no error, no rollback trace on our side, block-update broadcast just doesn't arrive in time) — including explaining the vanished chest (a logging/rollback mod reverting a change without cleanly returning the item is a known bug class for this mod family).

(a) ALL confirmed coords, collected from FEEDBACK (your 3 + 2 more I found):
- (18,89,60) — Grog, roof-rim, 5/5 fail, neighbor (19,89,60) worked first try
- (11,86,55) — Thak, 20/20 fail, directly under chest A, correlated with a real movement-freeze right after
- (12,91,53) — Grog, north lamppost torch, 2/2 fail
- (7,104,31) — Bonk, trade-path, 2/2 fail (2 techniques), neighbor (7,106,31) worked first try
- (10,89,55) — Grog, double-chest: 1st attempt SUCCEEDED, then 8/8 fails on re-attempts, then item vanished entirely on attempt #10

(b) world-feature mapping: 4 of 5 are within ~10 blocks of camp/chest-A (10,89,55 is literally adjacent to chest A; 11,86,55 is directly under it; 12,91,53 is next to chest B; 18,89,60 is at the Mine House roof edge) — BUT (7,104,31) is ~25+ blocks from camp, near the trade-path, breaking a clean "camp-radius protection" theory on geography alone. Chunk-boundary check: only (7,104,31) sits on a chunk edge (z=31, local z=15) — weak, not a pattern across all 5.

(c) live read-only probes (UngaBunga, idle, /eval blockAt — no placements): 3 of 5 (18,89,60 / 11,86,55 / 7,104,31) are STILL air right now, matching their "worked around, left unfilled" history exactly. 2 of 5 (12,91,53 now cobblestone, 10,89,55 now oak_planks) have since been filled by something — worth asking whoever last touched those spots whether it eventually worked or someone built over/around it.

STATIC-CODE FINDING, rules one theory OUT cleanly: read mineflayer's own placeBlock/onceWithCleanup source (node_modules). The FEEDBACK authors' leading theory ("listener dedup keyed on coordinates, leaking across repeated attempts") is NOT what's happening — onceWithCleanup's listener removal is in a .finally(), fires on timeout AND success, confirmed no leak. The exact error text ("Event blockUpdate did not fire within timeout of 5000ms") is mineflayer's own hardcoded string, not ours, and the wait only triggers when the bot's OWN local block cache doesn't already show the change immediately after the place packet — meaning the block genuinely never got confirmed by the server within 5s, from our side we can't tell if the server silently rejected it or just never broadcast the confirm. Consistent with a server-side interceptor (Ledger) being in the loop.

VERDICT: hypothesis = Ledger mod's block-change logging (possibly synchronous DB write, possibly contending under bursty placement activity near camp where most of our traffic is) intermittently delays/drops the block-update broadcast past our 5s wait, independent of technique/ref/face — explains every symptom including the item loss. Not proven — needs your Ledger config/log access to confirm, that's the natural next step, not something I can do from here.

FIX/WORKAROUND (regardless of Ledger root cause): a curse-coordinate registry is the right pragmatic move — cheap, bounded, and helps immediately whether or not Ledger turns out to be the cause. Sketch: a small `cave/curse-coords.json` (or reuse zones.json's shape) that safePlaceBlock checks before attempting; a known-bad coordinate gets ONE extra retry with a longer wait (mineflayer's 5s is baked into placeBlock itself, not ours to extend directly — would need to catch-and-retry, which we already do once) then auto-offsets to an adjacent cell instead of hammering the same coordinate (matches what Grog/Bonk already did by hand both times). Population: manual for now (the 5 known coords), or auto-add after N fails at one spot in a session. Small, bounded — happy to build once files unlock, not attempting now per your investigation-only scope.

Nothing else touched. Ready for whatever's next.
